title: Leviticus
introduction: Leviticus sets Israel’s worship, priesthood, purity, communal holiness, sacred times, land responsibilities and covenant obligations around the dwelling of God. These seven studies follow the book’s literary organization; they do not represent seven independently dated historical episodes. Historical reconstructions and later interpretations are identified as such.

entries.bookNote: Leviticus 1–7 sets out burnt, grain, well-being, purification, and reparation offerings and then priestly rules for their handling; the order is thematic, not an independently dated series.
Leviticus 8–10 narrates the installation of Aaron and his sons, the first public priestly service, and the deaths of Nadab and Abihu; the exact cause of their unauthorized fire remains unspecified.

Leviticus 11–15 prescribes animal classification, childbirth-related impurity, inspection and restoration for ṣāraʿat, and rules for bodily discharges. These are ritual categories, not automatic judgments of moral guilt.
Leviticus 16 details an annual sanctuary and communal atonement rite involving priestly entry, blood purification, and two goats with distinct functions, one sent alive into the wilderness.
Leviticus 17–22 joins restrictions on blood and sacrifice to laws of sexuality, justice, community care, priestly conduct, and acceptable offerings. Holiness integrates worship and daily conduct.
Leviticus 23–24 gathers weekly and annual sacred times, lamp and bread duties, and a legal narrative involving blasphemy, violence, and equal law.

Leviticus 25–27 concerns land Sabbath, Jubilee, redemption and servitude, covenant blessings and consequences, and a final set of vows and dedications; Jubilee practice is not independently established.
